Last updated: [date]

PopuliVerse collects as little personal data as it can. The site has no user accounts, no comments section, no advertising and no tracking cookies.

## Who is responsible

Khayyam Rzazade, editor of PopuliVerse. Contact: <hello@populiverse.com>.

## When you visit

**Hosting.** The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. To deliver the pages, GitHub processes technical data such as your IP address. [Link to GitHub's privacy statement.]

**Visit statistics.** [To confirm when analytics are switched on: Cloudflare Web Analytics, which counts visits without cookies.]

**Cookies.** The site itself sets no cookies.

**Fonts and scripts.** [To confirm with the final design: everything the pages need is served from this site, with nothing loaded from other companies.]

## When you give information

**Newsletter.** The newsletter runs on Substack. If you subscribe, Substack holds your email address and sends the emails. You can unsubscribe from any email. [Link to Substack's privacy policy.]

**Forms.** The "Suggest a paper" and contact forms run on Google Forms. What you enter is stored in the editor's Google account and is used only to consider the suggestion or to answer you. [Link to Google's privacy policy.]

**Email.** If you write to the editor, your message is kept for as long as it takes to deal with it.

**Commentary authors.** An author's name, affiliation and ORCID iD are published with the piece and deposited with it in Zenodo.

## Your rights

Under the EU's General Data Protection Regulation you can ask to see, correct or delete the personal data held about you, and you can complain to a data protection authority. To use these rights, write to the address above.

## Changes to this page

This page is updated whenever the site changes how it handles personal data.
